items.title: Topic Fourteen, Sub-Part 3: How Craving Forges Its Own Firm Bondage

items.zh: 眾生尋思所鑽搖，猛利貪欲隨觀妙；倍增染愛而流轉，便能自為堅固縛。
items.en: Beings, bored through and shaken by their own rumination, by fierce craving, by seeing things as inherently fine — their defiled longing doubling again and again as they drift on — thereby forge for themselves a truly firm bondage.

items.zh: 今此頌中，云何尋思之所鑽搖？謂如有一，於先所得、先所受用諸欲境界，不正作意，發生不善依於耽嗜諸惡尋思。云何猛利貪欲？謂如有一，於昔餘生修習貪欲，亦多修習；由是因緣，令此生中，於先所得、先所受用諸欲境界，雖正作意，而被貪欲散壞其心。云何隨觀淨妙？謂如有一，不善護身，不攝諸根，不住正念，遊行聚落，見甚少年可愛美色諸母邑已，便不如理取淨妙相；由此因緣，身心燒惱。云何倍增染愛？謂由五種相貌，當知染愛增長。何等為五？謂如有一，雖於下劣諸欲境界，尚生猛利諸貪欲纏，耽著不捨，何況上妙。又以非法多分凶暴積集珍財，不以正法，亦常攝受增上眾具。又於輕賤無所用物，尚不欲捨，何況貴重。雖為追求少劣財物，尚行眾多身語意惡，何況多勝。又於受持少小妙行，其心尚無趣向愛樂，何況廣大。又於涅槃尚不樂聞，何況欲得。云何堅固縛？謂由三種相，知堅固縛。一、堅牢故；二、苦所觸故；三、長時隨逐故。於現法中，由惡行根貪瞋癡故，知縛堅牢；於當來世，由生那落迦、傍生、鬼趣，知苦所觸及長時隨逐。復次，今當略辨上所說義。謂略顯示依二失壞因，有二種失壞。何等名為二失壞因？謂不正思惟力及因力。云何名為二種失壞？謂方求失壞及受用失壞。云何不正思惟力？謂隨念先所受用境界因緣所生不正思惟，或邪分別現前境界因緣所生不正思惟，或邪取相不正思惟，或即於彼若住、若行不正思惟。云何因力？謂於可愛境界宿習欲貪。云何方求失壞？謂如有一，成就二種失壞因故，以非正法，或以凶暴，追求積集所有邪財。云何受用失壞？謂如有一，於先所得順樂、順苦、順非苦樂諸境界中，或有於一生染、生著，廣說乃至不知出離而受用之。或有於一發生憎恚，憎恚所蔽。或有於一發生愚癡，愚癡所蔽。彼由如是貪染所蔽，乃至愚癡之所蔽故，行身語意種種惡行；為貪瞋癡三堅固縛之所纏縛，亦為那落迦、傍生、鬼等諸縛所縛。又有差別。謂愛結所繫補特伽羅，略有七種雜染，當知皆是貪愛所作。謂隨念雜染、不自在雜染、境界雜染、熱惱雜染、善趣相應雜染、惡趣相應雜染、諸見雜染。云何隨念雜染？謂如有一，不正隨念先所受用可愛境界，悕望追求，令心散壞。云何不自在雜染？謂如有一，宿世串習貪欲法故，今世貪欲為性猛利；雖復如理於可愛境隨念作意，而有悕望追求貪欲散壞其心。彼由貪欲極猛利故，心不自在。云何境界雜染？謂如有一，遊城邑等，現前會遇容色端嚴可愛境界；由彼境界極端嚴故，隨美妙相心識纏綿，因此發生悕望追求種種貪愛。云何熱惱雜染？謂如有一，由是三種能長貪愛諸雜染故，令已貪愛展轉增盛；追戀過去已受用境，悕求未來當受用境，耽著現在正受用境，乃令身心周遍熱惱。云何善趣相應雜染？謂即由彼貪愛集諦增上力故，行身語意種種妙行，得生善趣，或天、或人；彼於樂受耽著不捨，醉悶而住，專行放逸。云何惡趣相應雜染？謂即由彼貪愛集諦增上力故，行身語意種種惡行，身壞命終墮諸惡趣，生那落迦等；於彼生已，便為種種極重憂苦，惡心、憤心之所擾惱。云何諸見雜染？謂即由彼貪愛集諦增上力故，會遇惡友，說顛倒法，為令雜染得解脫故。彼雖悕求雜染解脫，由遇如是倒說法故，不證解脫。於六十二諸見趣中，隨令一種邪見增長；於諸緣起法，愚癡增上故。彼由如是見結所繫，於五趣等生死大海，不得解脫。
items.en: In this verse, what is being drilled and shaken by thoughts? Someone, attending incorrectly to objects of sense desire obtained and enjoyed before, gives rise to unwholesome, evil thoughts that depend on indulgence. What is intense sensual greed? Someone cultivated sensual greed in other past lives, and cultivated it much; because of this, in this life, even when they attend correctly to objects of sense desire obtained and enjoyed before, their mind is scattered and broken by sensual greed. What is observing the beautiful? Someone who does not guard the body well, does not restrain the senses, and does not abide in right mindfulness walks about the village, sees very young, lovely, beautiful women, and inappropriately grasps the sign of beauty; because of this, body and mind burn with torment. What is the redoubling of defiled craving? Defiled craving should be understood to grow through five features. What are the five? Someone gives rise to intense entanglements of sensual greed even towards inferior objects of sense desire, indulging in them and not letting go, let alone excellent ones. Further, they accumulate treasure and wealth by unlawful means, mostly violent, not by lawful means, and they constantly take on more and more possessions. Further, they do not wish to give up even worthless, useless things, let alone precious ones. Even in pursuing a little poor property, they commit many evil deeds of body, speech, and mind, let alone for much and good property. Further, their mind has no inclination or delight even in taking up a little good conduct, let alone extensive good conduct. Further, they do not even like to hear of nirvana, let alone wish to attain it. What is firm bondage? Firm bondage is known through three features: first, because it is strong; second, because it is touched by suffering; third, because it follows on for a long time. In this present life, the bondage is known to be strong because greed, anger, and delusion are the roots of bad conduct; in future lives, being born in the hells, as animals, or as ghosts, it is known to be touched by suffering and to follow on for a long time. Further, the meaning of what was said above will now be briefly set out. It briefly shows that, depending on two causes of ruin, there are two kinds of ruin. What are the two causes of ruin? The power of incorrect reflection and the power of causes. What are the two kinds of ruin? Ruin in seeking and ruin in enjoying. What is the power of incorrect reflection? It is incorrect reflection born from recollecting objects enjoyed before, or incorrect reflection born from wrongly discriminating objects present now, or incorrect reflection that wrongly grasps signs, or incorrect reflection while standing or walking among them. What is the power of causes? It is sensual greed for attractive objects habituated in past lives. What is ruin in seeking? Someone, having the two causes of ruin, pursues and accumulates wrong wealth by unlawful or violent means. What is ruin in enjoying? Someone, among objects obtained before that lead to pleasure, pain, or neither, becomes defiled by and attached to one of them, and so on at length up to enjoying it without knowing the escape. Or towards one of them they give rise to hatred and are obscured by hatred; or towards one of them they give rise to delusion and are obscured by delusion. Because they are obscured by greed, and so on up to delusion, they commit all kinds of bad conduct of body, speech, and mind; they are bound by the three firm bonds of greed, anger, and delusion, and also by the bonds of the hells, animals, ghosts, and so on. There is a further distinction: a person bound by the fetter of craving has, in brief, seven kinds of defilement, all of which should be understood as the work of craving. They are the defilement of recollection, the defilement of lack of mastery, the defilement of objects, the defilement of torment, the defilement connected with good destinies, the defilement connected with bad destinies, and the defilement of views. What is the defilement of recollection? Someone incorrectly recollects attractive objects enjoyed before, longs for them, pursues them, and lets the mind be scattered and broken. What is the defilement of lack of mastery? Someone, through habituation to sensual greed in past lives, now has an intense nature of sensual greed; even when they recollect and attend appropriately to attractive objects, longing and pursuit of sensual greed scatter and break their mind. Because their sensual greed is extremely intense, their mind lacks mastery. What is the defilement of objects? Someone walks about towns and villages and meets in front of them attractive objects of fine and beautiful appearance; because those objects are extremely beautiful, their mind clings to the beautiful features, and from this all kinds of craving, longing, and pursuit arise. What is the defilement of torment? Someone, through these three defilements that increase craving, makes the craving they already have grow ever stronger; they long for objects enjoyed in the past, hope for objects to be enjoyed in the future, and indulge in objects being enjoyed now, so that body and mind are tormented throughout. What is the defilement connected with good destinies? Through the dominant force of that craving, the truth of origination, they practise various kinds of good conduct of body, speech, and mind and are born in a good destiny, as a god or a human; there they indulge in pleasant feeling and do not let go, live intoxicated, and give themselves wholly to heedlessness. What is the defilement connected with bad destinies? Through the dominant force of that craving, the truth of origination, they commit various kinds of bad conduct of body, speech, and mind, and when the body breaks up at death they fall into bad destinies and are born in the hells and so on; once born there, they are troubled by all kinds of extremely heavy sorrow and pain, malice, and resentment. What is the defilement of views? Through the dominant force of that craving, the truth of origination, they meet bad friends who teach inverted doctrines as a way to be liberated from defilement. Although they long to be liberated from defilement, because they have met such inverted teaching, they do not realise liberation. Among the sixty-two views, one wrong view or another is made to grow, because delusion about the dharmas of dependent arising predominates. Bound by this fetter of views, they are not liberated from the great ocean of birth and death of the five destinies.

blocks.text: One verse and a long explanation, **almost all missing from Ru-Yi's translation** (0379b26–0380b09). The explanation analyses, step by step, how craving builds its own prison. The English column gives our own translation.
"Beings, bored through and shaken by their own rumination, by fierce craving, by seeing things as fine, their defiled longing doubling again and again, thereby forge for themselves a firm bondage."

items: **Rumination** is improper attention to pleasures already had, producing unwholesome, indulgent thoughts.

**Fierce craving** comes from having cultivated desire in past lives, so that even with proper attention desire scatters the mind. Venerable Miào Jìng: someone reborn from the higher realms may have lighter afflictions.

**Seeing things as fine**: walking through a village without guarding body, senses, or mindfulness, one sees an attractive person and grasps the lovely mark, and body and mind burn. Master Cháng Bǎi: "beautiful or not is a manifestation of mind only"; the craving makes the object seem lovely.

**Doubling longing** shows in five ways: strong craving even for inferior things; gaining wealth by wrong means; unwillingness to give up even useless things; doing much wrong for small gains; and no interest in wholesome practice, nor even in hearing of nirvāṇa.
**Firm bondage** has three marks: it is firm (rooted in greed, hatred, delusion now), painful (rebirth in hell, as an animal or ghost), and long-lasting.

**Two causes, two ruins.** The causes are improper attention and past habit. The ruins are in **seeking** (acquiring wealth by wrong means) and in **using** (craving, hatred, or delusion towards what one has).

**Seven defilements of craving:** recollection (of past pleasures); lack of control (from past habit); objects (meeting attractive forms); burning (craving grows, longing for past, future, present); good destinies (born in heaven, one becomes intoxicated with pleasure); bad destinies (born in hell, one is tormented); and views (meeting bad teachers, one adopts one of the sixty-two views and stays bound in saṃsāra).

blocks.text: This is a diagnostic passage. It shows craving as a process with stages, each of which can be noticed. Master Cháng Bǎi: "the firm bondage" is first of all affliction itself, very hard to destroy, and one forges it oneself.

quiz.q: According to the verse, how do beings forge a firm bondage for themselves?
options: bored through and shaken by rumination, by fierce craving, by seeing things as fine, their defiled longing doubling as they drift on
quiz.why: Beings, bored through and shaken by rumination, by fierce craving, by seeing things as fine, their defiled longing doubling as they drift on, thereby forge for themselves a firm bondage. Master Cháng Bǎi: the firm bondage refers first to affliction, which is very firm and hard to break.

quiz.q: "Seeing things as fine" — is it the lovely object that binds a person? What do the two masters say?
options: yes, the object itself is the rope
yes, so lovely things should be destroyed
no — Cháng Bǎi: beauty is mind-only, appearing because one's own craving arises; Miào Jìng: the lovely mark does not bind — the affliction of craving for it does
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: beautiful or not is a manifestation of mind only; it is the craving in one's own mind that makes her seem lovely — the object itself is neither good nor bad. Venerable Miào Jìng: in fact the lovely mark does not bind anyone; it is the affliction of craving for it that binds.

quiz.q: Which phrases of the verse does Master Cháng Bǎi assign to "the power of improper reflection"?
options: the first line's rumination, plus "seeing as fine" and "doubling of defiled longing"; fierce craving belongs to the power of past causes
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: first, the power of improper reflection is the verse's first line — beings bored through by rumination — together with "seeing as fine" in the second line and "doubling of defiled longing" in the third. Fierce craving belongs to the power of causes habituated in past lives.

quiz.q: What does Master Cháng Bǎi say is the first meaning of "firm bondage"?
options: affliction — very firm and hard to break
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the firm bondage refers to affliction; the first sense of firm bondage is affliction, which is very firm and hard to destroy.

quiz.q: How does Venerable Miào Jìng relate the strength of "fierce craving" to one's previous life?
options: if one was in the form or formless heavens last life, one's afflictions in the desire realm now are lighter
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: if someone was in the form or formless heavens in the previous life, then coming to the desire realm in this life, their afflictions are lighter. Fierce craving belongs to the power of past causes and varies with past habituation.
